title: Petro Alleges Election Fraud, Accuses Israel and US of Interference
detail: Outgoing President Gustavo Petro refused to recognize the June 21 runoff result, alleging systematic tampering with Form E-14 tally sheets and claiming Israel had compromised National Registry servers used by electoral logistics firm Thomas Greg & Sons — telling reporters 'the only entity in the world capable of doing that is the state of Israel.' Petro invited US President Trump to mediate the dispute. Attorney General Gregorio Eljach dismissed the claims, stating there was 'no evidence of fraud' with 99% of votes counted. De la Espriella, a pro-Israel candidate who pledged to reverse Petro's 2024 rupture of diplomatic ties with Israel, received a congratulatory message from Israeli PM Netanyahu.

media.caption: Colombia gripped by tension as President Petro alleges fraud in razor-thin election

title: De la Espriella Holds First Meeting to Decide Cabinet Ministers
detail: Days after his runoff win, President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella held his first formal meeting to begin deciding cabinet appointments, launching a selection process centered on a hard-line security posture that breaks from Petro's 'Total Peace' approach.
